source_neutral.procedure: Assemble a proposed reference series of comparable correspondence from the same creator and relevant context, in which each item is independently dated and the items are placed in chronological order. The physical arrangement of the undated bundle is not used as the order of writing. Select a two-state feature (absent or present) that can be inspected reproducibly, for example a particular address printed on letterhead, such that an earlier reference demonstrably lacks it and a later reference displays it. The procedure assumes that the feature changed state once and then persisted throughout the applicable correspondence; the packet establishes neither this assumption nor the existence of suitable references. Reference dates must constrain the date of writing, and the precision of each date is recorded; postmarks or accession dates alone do not automatically supply writing dates. The overall process repeatedly inspects an intermediate reference between the two retained endpoints to shrink the span of the reference series in which the hypothesized change of state lies, then classifies the undated documents by the same feature rule and derives relative order and date bounds conditionally.
source_neutral.action: 1) Inspect a reference near the middle of the remaining ordered interval, applying a fixed rule for deciding feature presence. 2) If the feature is clearly absent, make that reference the earlier endpoint; if clearly present, make it the later endpoint. 3) Set aside the half of the interval that is incompatible with the result, doing so solely under the single-transition assumption. 4) Repeat until the absent and present classifications belong to adjacent references in the available series. 5) If a reference cannot be classified or cannot be securely ordered, record its uncertainty and inspect a different intermediate reference; stop narrowing when no usable intermediate reference remains. 6) Inspect the undated documents with the same feature rule, restricting comparison to documents whose creator, context and feature meaning are sufficiently comparable to the references. 7) Record for each inspected item its classification, date constraint and the visible evidence supporting the classification.
source_neutral.observables: For each usable reference: a classification of absent or present, its date constraint with stated precision, and the visible evidence supporting the classification. Across iterations: the retained earlier and later endpoints, which progressively narrow the reference interval containing the hypothesized transition. Illegibility, missing portions, incompatible dates, or an absence in a later reference after a presence in an earlier reference are recorded as uncertainty or contradiction and are not forced into one of the two classes. For undated documents: a feature classification; the inspection does not yield a date directly.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: If the endpoints are reliable and the feature underwent a single persistent transition, the final boundary identifies the first feature-positive reference in the applicable series and places the transition between the last feature-negative reference and the first feature-positive reference, subject to the precision of their dates. It does not identify the exact historical date of introduction within an undocumented gap between those two references. If independent evidence supports that the two feature states were used contemporaneously with their periods and exclusively, feature-negative undated letters precede feature-positive undated letters; no order is established among letters within either group. A feature-negative letter receives an upper date bound taken from the positive endpoint; a feature-positive letter receives a lower date bound taken from the negative endpoint. Neither group is thereby confined to the transition interval. These bounds may be combined with independently justified dating clues when the two are compatible, and open or uncertain intervals are retained. A feature boundary can correlate with a historical change without proving the cause of that change.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: (a) the reference series, consisting of comparable, independently dated items from the same creator and context, each with a date constraint and precision; (b) the chosen two-state feature and the fixed rule for classifying it; (c) the two retained endpoints, one feature-negative and earlier, one feature-positive and later, and the remaining interval between them; (d) the undated bundle documents, each assessed for comparability and then classified by the feature; (e) independently justified dating clues and anchors external to the feature. Relationships: the ordered reference series, together with the single-transition assumption, links feature state to position in time; the endpoints bracket the transition; the classification of an undated document links it to one side of the bracket, giving relative order between the two feature groups and one-sided date bounds (upper for negative, lower for positive), conditional on independent support for contemporaneous, exclusive use of the feature states. Relative chronology is addressed between groups and not within them; absolute chronology is addressed through one-sided bounds and their compatible combination with independent clues.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: When a reference cannot be classified or securely ordered, inspect another intermediate reference. When contradictory evidence appears, check the conflicting classifications, the dates and the comparability of the items involved. Seek independent dating anchors or additional comparable documents. Where a reliable ordered series with opposite endpoints cannot be established, seek independent dating anchors. Combine the feature-derived bounds with independently justified dating clues where compatible. No further follow-up beyond these steps is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions that can invalidate the elimination of part of the interval or prevent a unique localization of the transition: reused stationery, addresses in parallel use, differing correspondents or contexts, more than one transition, missing references, unreliable dates, and inconsistent inspection. Inspecting a sparse set of intermediate references cannot establish that the feature persisted after its change. The single-transition assumption and the existence of suitable references are not established by the packet. Postmarks or accession dates alone do not automatically supply writing dates. The result does not give the exact historical introduction date across an undocumented gap, does not order letters within a feature group, does not confine either group to the transition interval, and does not prove the cause of any correlated historical change. Stopping and suspension rules: stop narrowing when the opposite classifications belong to adjacent references in the available series; stop narrowing when no usable intermediate reference remains; if contradictory evidence appears, suspend the affected elimination and restore the possibilities that had been excluded; retain alternative chronologies when conflicts remain; without support for exclusive contemporaneous use of the feature states, report the observed reference boundary and conditional dating hypotheses for the bundle and nothing further; if a reliable ordered series and opposite endpoints cannot be established, do not carry out the interval-halving procedure and preserve unresolved intervals.
